claim: Scrovegni Chapel full-price daytime ticket is €15 plus €1 presale fee; reduced €11, youth/student €6, special evening ticket €9; same-day bookings not accepted.
quote: Full Price: €15 + €1 presale fee (adults 18+)... Reduced: €11 + €1 presale fee... Youth/Students: €6 + €1 presale fee... Full Price Evening: €9 + €1 presale fee... it is not possible to make reservations for the same day

claim: Scrovegni Chapel visits last exactly 15 minutes, visitors must reach the air-conditioned waiting room 5 minutes before the slot, and automatic doors open only once on entry and exit to stabilise the interior microclimate.
quote: Scrovegni Chapel visits last 15 minutes... visitors must arrive at the air-conditioned waiting room entrance 5 minutes before the visit time printed on their tickets... automatic doors open only once upon entrance and exit, to enable the stabilisation of the interior microclimate

claim: The Padova Urbs Picta combined card costs €28 for 48 hours or €35 for 72 hours, includes unlimited public transport, and covers all eight UNESCO 14th-century fresco sites with one entry per site.
quote: 48-hour ticket: €28; 72-hour ticket: €35; Provincial resident pass: €25 (valid 6 months). Each ticket permits one entry per site and includes unlimited public transportation access

claim: The eight Urbs Picta UNESCO sites are the Scrovegni Chapel, Church of Saints Philip and James in the Eremitani, Palazzo della Ragione, Baptistery of the Cathedral, Chapel of the Carrarese Palace, Basilica and Convent of Sant'Antonio, Oratory of San Giorgio, and Oratory of San Michele.
quote: The sites include the Scrovegni Chapel; Church of Saints Philip and James in the Eremitani; Palazzo della Ragione; Baptistery of the Cathedral; Chapel of the Carrarese Palace; Basilica and Convent of Sant Antonio, Oratory of San Giorgio and the Oratory of San Michele

claim: Basilica of Saint Anthony requires church-appropriate attire, prohibits all photography, animals, food and drink inside; audioguides and disabled access are available.
quote: clothing that is suitable to a church environment... The use of photographic equipment of any kind is prohibited... Animals of any size are not allowed within the Basilica... No food or beverages permitted inside

claim: Basilica of Saint Anthony is open daily from 06:20 to 19:45 in summer and 06:20 to 19:00 in winter, with entry free of charge.
quote: The basilica is open from 06:20 until 19:45 in summer and from 06:20 until 19:00 in winter

claim: Orto Botanico di Padova full ticket is €10, over-65 €8, youth €6, family (2 adults + up to 3 children) €25; last admission 45 minutes before closing.
quote: Full ticket: €10.00, Over 65: €8.00, Special reduced youth ticket: €6.00, Children (0-5 years): free, Family ticket (2 adults + up to 3 children): €25.00... Last admission is 45 minutes before closing time

claim: Palazzo della Ragione opens Tuesday-Sunday 09:00-19:00 (last entry 30 min before closing), full ticket €8 / reduced €6, and its ground floor is the oldest covered market in Europe at over 800 years old.
quote: open from Tuesday to Sunday, 9:00 AM to 7:00 PM, with last entry 30 minutes before closing... full ticket price is €8.00... the ground floor of Palazzo della Ragione houses the oldest covered market in Europe, which has been active for more than 800 years

claim: Prato della Valle is a 90,000 m² elliptical square with 78 statues in two concentric rings around the canal-bordered Isola Memmia, hosting a 160-stall Saturday market and an antiques market every third Sunday.
quote: 90,000-square-meter elliptical square... 78 statues (40 in the exterior ring and 38 statues in the inner ring)... Every Saturday is held a traditional market with over 160 stalls, while the antique market takes place every third Sunday

claim: Caffè Pedrocchi's Piano Nobile housing the Museo del Risorgimento opens Tuesday-Sunday 09:30-12:30 and 15:30-18:00 with a €4 ticket; the café itself runs 08:00 to midnight daily, free to enter.
quote: Museum of the Risorgimento is open from Tuesday to Sunday, from 9.30 to 12.30 and from 15.30 to 18.00... The ticket costs €4.00 and includes access to the Pedrocchi Noble Floor

claim: Prato della Valle was reclaimed from swampland in 1775 under Venetian Provveditore Andrea Memmo to a design by architect Domenico Cerato; its statues honour figures including Galileo, Petrarch, Ariosto and Copernicus.
quote: in 1775, Andrea Memmo, the city's Venetian Superintendent, decided to reclaim and restore this area of Padua... He commissioned Domenico Cerato... Key individuals immortalized in these sculptures include authors Ludovico Ariosto and Francesco Petrarch and scientists Galileo Galilei and Nicolaus Copernicus

claim: The Euganean Hills Regional Park covers about 18,694 hectares, was established in 1989, has Monte Venda (601 m) as its highest peak, hills of volcanic origin from ~35 million years ago, and spans 15 municipalities.
quote: The park encompasses around 18,694 hectares ... established in 1989. The hills are of volcanic origin created around 35 million years ago (Oligocene). Mount Venda, at 601 m above sea level, is the highest one.

claim: The Colli Euganei comprise about 81 distinctive volcanic hills rising abruptly from the Po plain southwest of Padua.
quote: The Colli Euganei ... form the first Regional Park established in Veneto (1989), occupying an area with a roughly elliptical perimeter ... comprising 81 hills and fifteen municipalities.

claim: Trail No. 9 to Monte Venda is an easy 3.5 km route with only 66 m elevation gain, walkable in under 1.5 hours from Casa Marina visitor centre in Galzignano Terme.
quote: Trail No. 9 is suitable for all, has a length of approximately 3.5 km, limited elevation gain of 66 meters, and requires less than 1.5 hours of walking.

claim: Trail No. 4 (Sentiero G.G. Lorenzoni) is the more challenging Monte Venda loop, ~6 km with 250 m elevation gain, ~2.5 hours, passing the ruined Olivetan monastery near the summit.
quote: loop trail of medium difficulty, approximately 6 km long, with 250 meters of elevation gain and an estimated travel time of 2.5 hours (3 hours with a detour to monastery ruins).

claim: The Alta Via dei Colli Euganei is a 42 km long-distance ridge route with 2,000 m total elevation gain, demanding but technically non-difficult.
quote: The Alta Via dei Colli Euganei, a demanding hike of 42 km with 2,000 m elevation gain that does not require particular technical skills but requires fair training.

claim: Arquà Petrarca preserves the house where Francesco Petrarch lived 1369–1374 until his death, now a museum with frescoed rooms and personal artefacts.
quote: The house where Francesco Petrarch spent his final days has been preserved as it once was ... Francesco Petrarch stayed in the last years of his life, from 1369 to 1374.

claim: Beyond the poet's house and red Verona marble sarcophagus tomb in Santa Maria Assunta churchyard, Arquà has the 12th-century Oratorio SS Trinità, an ancient fountain, and the nearby baroque Valsanzibio garden.
quote: Oratorio SS Trinità e Loggia dei Vicari ... Located at the highest part of town, this 12th-century oratory features the magnificent altar piece by Palma il Giovane.

claim: Arquà Petrarca was named Borgo dei Borghi (Italy's most beautiful village) in 2017, signalling broad popularity with tourists.
quote: In 2017, Arquà Petrarca won the title of Borgo dei Borghi (the best hamlet in Italy).

claim: Abbazia di Praglia, the Benedictine abbey in Teolo, opens to guided visits Mon–Fri 15:00–17:00 and Sat–Sun 15:30–17:30, free with suggested donation (~€5), and the monumental library opens only on the 2nd and 4th Saturday of each month.
quote: Regular opening hours are Monday-Friday 3-5 PM; Saturday 3:30-5:30 PM; Sunday 3:30-5:30 PM ... Access to the monumental library is available on the second and fourth Saturday of each month.

claim: Eremo di Monte Rua is a Camaldolese hermitage at 416 m on a summit above Torreglia, founded in 1339, with 14 cloistered monks' cells, and access restricted to men only outside of Jubilee years.
quote: located on the summit of Monte Rua (416 m above sea level) in the municipality of Torreglia ... A small community of cloistered Camaldolese monks lives here ... access is restricted ... precluded to women.

claim: The Colli Euganei DOC wine zone covers ~1,300 hectares on calcareous and volcanic slopes around Arquà Petrarca, Galzignano Terme and Torreglia, producing reds (Merlot, Cabernet) and the aromatic Fior d'Arancio DOCG.
quote: Colli Euganei is a DOC area ... covers around 1,300 hectares of vineyards on volcanic and highly calcareous mountain slopes ... includes the municipalities of Arquà Petrarca, Galzignano Terme and Torreglia.

claim: The signature Colli Euganei cycling loop is roughly 63 km, mostly flat on bike lanes, encircling the hills through Padova, Este, Abano and Montegrotto Terme — doable in a day.
quote: nearly 63 km almost completely through a bicycle lane with a wonderful view of the Euganean Hills, an easy ride, mostly flat, especially recommended in Spring, Summer and Fall.

claim: Abano and Montegrotto Terme together form Europe's largest and oldest thermal spa district, with over 130 thermal hotels offering day-spa access from roughly €85 per person.
quote: the Thermal Baths of Abano and Montegrotto are the largest and oldest thermal spa in Europe ... Over 130 thermal spas and around 220 baths.

claim: April–May is the prime window for the Colli Euganei: mild 15–20 °C temperatures, blooming wildflowers, plus seasonal sagre and wine festivals tied to the DOC/DOCG.
quote: In spring, mild temperatures (around 15–20°C) and wildflower blooms make it perfect for gentle explorations, short hikes, and village-hopping by car, bike, or e-bike.

claim: A typical car loop strings together Este's 14th-century castle, the Cava Bomba geo-paleontological museum near Cinto Euganeo, Castello di Valbona on Monte Lozzo, Abbazia di Praglia, and the Abano/Montegrotto thermal towns.
quote: Este, with its 14th-century castle and panoramic views of the hills ... the Geo-Paleontological Museum of Cava Bomba near Cinto Euganeo ... Castello di Valbona ... Abbadia di Praglia ... thermal baths of Abano and Montegrotto.

claim: The Euganean thermal water springs at 87°C, is classified as hyperthermal salso-bromo-iodic, and is unique in the world.
quote: The meteoric waters spring forth at a constant temperature of 87°C and are unique in the world... classified, from a chemical point of view, as hyperthermal, sodium-chloride, and... as salso-bromo-iodic with a fixed residue at 180° of 5-6 grams of dissolved salts per liter.

claim: Abano/Montegrotto fango is matured 60+ days in thermal water and contains the patented Phormidium ETS05 cyanobacterium responsible for its anti-inflammatory effect.
quote: The Euganean thermal clay contains a particular type of microalgae, the cyanobacteria Phormidium SP ETS05, which is deposited at the Institut Pasteur in Paris and is protected by a European patent.

claim: Y-40 The Deep Joy in Montegrotto lets non-divers walk a submerged transparent tunnel at -5 m and watch from the bar-bistro windows for free; divers must pre-register online with a QR code.
quote: watch the dives for free from the windows of the bar-bistro and from the underwater tunnel at -5 meters depth... All participants must register online, complete health disclosures, and generate QR codes before arrival.

claim: Y-40 holds 4.3 million litres of salso-bromo-iodic thermal water kept at 32–34°C with a maximum depth of 42.15 m — the deepest thermal pool in the world.
quote: Y-40 The Deep Joy has a surface area of 21x18m, a maximum depth of 42.15 meters... The pool holds 4,300,000 liters of salsobromoiodic thermal water, maintained at a temperature of 32-34°C.

claim: Hotel Mioni Pezzato in Abano sells a pool-only Spa Day from €75 (Mon-Thu) and massage-included packages at €120–155, open 8 am–9 pm, reservation mandatory.
quote: Spa Day 1: €75 (Mon-Thu) - Pool & spa access only... Access to and stay in the structure are allowed from 8 a.m. until 9 p.m... Spa Day tickets are available by reservation only and subject to availability.

claim: Day-pass prices across the basin range from €13–15 at Hotel Smeraldo/Milano (Abano) up to €40–45 at Hotel Mioni Royal San (Montegrotto), with €6–7 municipal pools also available.
quote: Hotel Smeraldo (3-star) Daily: €15 (Mon-Fri), €18 (Sat-Sun)... Hotel Mioni Royal San (4-star) Daily: €40 (Mon-Thu), €45 (Fri-Sun)... Piscine Comunali Daily: €6-€7.

claim: Terme Preistoriche in Montegrotto runs an adults-only Day Spa from October to March, online-booking only, with bathrobe and towel kit included.
quote: From 1 October to 31 March access to the Day Spa is reserved for guests over 16 years of age... The SPA KIT, which includes a bathrobe and towel, is included with every type of entry... Access to the facility is by reservation only.

claim: Hotel Savoia Thermae in Abano offers a Saturday day pass at €65 (€55 weekday) and an afternoon-only 14:00–22:00 entry from €35.
quote: Mon-Fri €55.00, Sat-Sun €65.00, Public holidays €85.00 for full wellness without overnight stay... Afternoon relaxation (2:00 PM to 10:00 PM) starting from €35.

claim: Visitors describe Abano as the livelier town with more shops, bars and hotels, while Montegrotto is a quieter walkable village next to the rail station and Roman archaeological area.
quote: Abano: more lively village, lots of shops, bars, more hotels on offer... Montegrotto: smaller village, railway station at a walkable distance, original roman SPAs location... not much to see do around (it's a sleepy village).

claim: The thermal water makes a 25-year underground journey from the Dolomites before surfacing at 87°C, and the Euganean fango is the regional curative speciality.
quote: The thermal water travels from the Lower Dolomites through a 25-year underground journey, soaking up mineral salts before gushing out at a temperature of 87°C... The mud here is so valued that the European Patent Office has declared it a drug.

claim: Fango is applied to the skin at 37–42°C for around 15 minutes and was clinically shown by the Centro Studi Termali Pietro D'Abano to match NSAIDs for anti-inflammatory effect without GI side-effects.
quote: The mud is applied directly to the skin and left for about 15 minutes at a temperature ranging between 37 °C and 42 °C... the mature fango therapy of Abano and Montegrotto Terme is as effective against inflammation as NSAID-based drug therapy, but without side effects on the gastrointestinal tract.

claim: Casa del Petrarca in Arquà preserves the poet's study, library, chair and famous stuffed cat in a 13th-century house with 14th-century features and 16th-century frescoes of Petrarch's works; admission €5 full / €3 reduced, summer hours 09:00-12:30 and 15:00-19:00, winter 09:00-12:30 and 14:30-17:30, last entry 30 min before closing.
quote: The house is a 13th-century building that maintains most of its original 14th-century features. In the 16th century, a loggia was added and rooms were frescoed with scenes inspired by Petrarch's most famous works.

claim: Arquà Petrarca is officially in the Borghi più Belli d'Italia network; Petrarch's red Verona-marble tomb stands in the middle of the churchyard of Santa Maria Assunta (built six years after his death), and notable buildings include 15th-c Venetian Gothic Palazzo Contarini and the Loggia dei Vicari at the Oratory of the Santissima Trinità.
quote: The light colored stone of the buildings, its churches and its town houses (built for the rich Venetian families) are surrounded by an atmosphere of peace and serenity.

claim: The Festa delle Giuggiole runs the first two Sundays of October (5 and 12 October 2025 for the 45th edition) and turns the village into an open-air medieval reenactment with flag-bearers, drummers and costumed Petrarch and Laura; jujubes thrive on Euganean Hills microclimate and are preserved in syrup or sweet 'brodo di giuggiole' wine.
quote: Per due domeniche – 5 e 12 ottobre 2025 – il borgo che fu dimora di Petrarca si trasforma in un palcoscenico a cielo aperto, animato da cultura, sapori e rievocazioni storiche.

claim: Castello di Monselice (Castello Cini) is visited only by guided tour of about 60 minutes; full ticket €10, reduced €7, family €20, children 6-14 €5; open March-October at 9/10/11 and 15/16/17, November-February at 10/11 and 14/15; closed Tuesdays.
quote: Full ticket: €10.00 ... The castle visit lasts approximately 60 minutes and is always guided ... Closed: Tuesdays (except public holidays like June 2)

claim: Count Vittorio Cini furnished the medieval castle with an exceptional collection of armour, tapestries, period furniture and Renaissance artefacts, turning Castello di Monselice into a living museum of Italian decorative arts.
quote: Count Cini furnished the interiors with an exceptional collection of medieval and Renaissance artefacts, armour, tapestries, and period furniture, transforming the castle into a living museum of Italian decorative arts.

claim: The Giostra della Rocca, Monselice's medieval festival, fills the first three weeks of September commemorating Frederick II of Swabia's 1239 stay; events include a historic parade, medieval market, chess tournament on a human-piece square, archery, millstone strength trials, and the Quintana joust on the third Sunday afternoon on Via Piave.
quote: The Giostra della Rocca includes archery competitions, proof of strength at the millstones, a relay race, the chess tournament, the Quintana horse racing, the reenactment of medieval arts and crafts, the Tenzone and a spectacular parade (Corteo).

claim: The Santuario delle Sette Chiese is a 1605-1615 Vincenzo Scamozzi pilgrimage route of six chapels climbing the hill to the church of San Giorgio next to Villa Duodo; Pope Paul V granted plenary indulgence equivalent to visiting Rome's seven basilicas, and Palma il Giovane painted the six chapel altarpieces depicting the Roman basilicas.
quote: In 1605 he received permission from Pope Paul V to build and name the small churches after the seven imposing basilicas in Rome, obtaining the same privilege as a plenary indulgence.

claim: Access to the Seven Churches walk through the Porta Romana is free; the gateway opens 9:00-12:00 and 14:00-17:00 (15:00-18:00 in daylight saving time), the walk takes under two hours from Piazza Mazzini past Castello Cini and the Pieve of Santa Giustina, with Villa Duodo itself closed to the public.
quote: The gateway to the Sanctuary is open daily from 9:00 AM to 12:00 PM and from 2:00 PM to 5:00 PM (during daylight saving time from 3:00 PM to 6:00 PM).

claim: Este's Castello Carrarese, rebuilt 1339 by Ubertino da Carrara, retains about 1 km of crenellated walls with 12 towers and two keeps; the Mocenigo family added a palace on the south side around 1570 that now houses the Museo Nazionale Atestino, and the interior is laid out as well-kept public gardens opened in 1915.
quote: remains of the original structure include a city wall with a perimeter of over one thousand meters, from which twelve towers rise separated by crenellated curtains, plus two imposing keeps

claim: The Museo Nazionale Atestino in Palazzo Mocenigo holds the most important collection of pre-Roman Veneti culture in Italy, with the 7th-century-BC bronze Situla Benvenuti as its showpiece — a vessel covered in engraved figural friezes that is among the masterworks of Atestine 'situla art'.
quote: The museum hosts the most representative archaeological materials of the culture of the Veneti, who inhabited the region throughout the entire 1st millennium BC.

claim: Museo Nazionale Atestino admission is €5 full / €4 reduced (ARTE TERME CARD); the museum is open Tuesday-Saturday 08:30-19:30 plus first and third Sundays of the month, closed Mondays, 25 December, 1 January and 1 May; currently undergoing PNRR-funded renovation.
quote: The full adult ticket price is €5.00, with a discounted rate of €4.00 for ARTE TERME CARD holders.

claim: A single-day driving loop links the three towns naturally: Battaglia Terme → Monselice (castle hill stratified from Federician Mastio and Ezzeliana tower up to Renaissance Villa Duodo and the Sette Chiese) → Arquà Petrarca via vineyards and olive groves → Este as the 'cradle of ancient Venetian civilization'.
quote: You can discover the walled towns of the Euganean Hills (Monselice and Este) and the medieval village of Arquà Petrarca in one day.

claim: Montagnana sits about 50 km from Padua (outside a 30-km Rubano radius) but is worth noting for its nearly intact 2-km circuit of medieval walls punctuated by 24 hexagonal towers up to 19 m high, with the Rocca degli Alberi keep at the west gate and Castello di San Zeno on the east, completed around 1360 under Francesco il Vecchio da Carrara.
quote: The two kilometres of medieval walls interrupted by 24 majestic hexagonal towers up to 19 meters high are the flagship of Montagnana, a defensive outpost since ancient times.

claim: Visitor accounts consistently rate Arquà Petrarca the most atmospheric of the trio for its preserved medieval stone village setting and Petrarch associations, while Monselice's draw is the layered castle-hill ascent up the Via del Santuario; Este is treated as the historical/archaeological complement.
quote: Monselice and Arqua Petrarca: Two North Italian villages worth visiting

claim: Villa Pisani museum opens Tue-Sun 9:00-20:00; ticket €9 full, €6 reduced, €2 youth 18-25; park and maze closed until June 2026 for PNRR restoration.
quote: DAL MARTEDì ALLA DOMENICA: dalle ore 9:00 alle ore 20:00 ... Il parco monumentale e il labirinto resteranno chiusi al pubblico fino al completamento degli interventi richiesti dai lavori del PNRR in corso, previsto per il mese di Giugno 2026.

claim: The Apotheosis of the Pisani Family by Giambattista Tiepolo (1760-62), in the ballroom of Villa Pisani Stra, is Tiepolo's largest fresco for a private residence and his last work in Italy.
quote: The Apotheosis of the Pisani Family, Giambattista Tiepolo's masterpiece decorating the ballroom of Villa Pisani in Stra, is his largest fresco painting for a private residence.

claim: Villa Pisani was begun in 1721 by the Pisani di Santo Stefano; Napoleon bought it in the early 19th century and famously got lost in the boxwood labyrinth in 1807.
quote: Villa Pisani, erected beginning in 1721 ... Napoleon Bonaparte purchased the villa ... in 1807, got completely lost in the labyrinth and had to be rescued by his guards.

claim: Valsanzibio garden 2026 season runs Sat 21 Feb to Tue 8 Dec; daily 10:00 to sunset; adult €14, children €7.50; boxwood maze access requires €4 supplement.
quote: Stagione 2026, SABATO 21/02 – MARTEDI' 8/12 ... dalle 10:00 al tramonto ... Adults: €14.00 ... Boxwood maze supplement: €4.00 per adult

claim: Villa Barbarigo's Baroque garden was commissioned 1669, voted Italy's most beautiful garden in 2003; its boxwood labyrinth uses ~6,000 plants mostly planted 1664-1669, making it one of the oldest surviving mazes.
quote: The baroque garden of the Villa Barbarigo has been voted as 'Italy's most beautiful garden' in 2003 ... The labyrinth is comprised of six thousand Boxwood plants, with the majority of these plants being over 400 years old as they were planted between 1664-1669

claim: Villa Foscari 'La Malcontenta' opens from 1 April Tue/Wed/Fri/Sat/Sun 9-12 and 14:30-17:30, Thu 9-12; March 2026 limited to dates 15, 21-22, 28-29; tickets €15 full, €10 students, €30 family.
quote: Tuesday, Wednesday, Friday, Saturday, Sunday: from 9am to 12pm and from 2.30pm to 5.30pm ... Thursday from 9am to 12pm ... € 15 : full regular ... € 30 FAMILY TICKET

claim: Il Burchiello full-day Padova-Venezia cruise runs 14 March to 1 November 2026, Wed/Fri/Sat/Sun, 8:00-17:30 from Portello, €147 adult / €59 child, visiting Villa Pisani, Villa Widmann, and Villa Foscari.
quote: Cruises are available from March 14th to November 1st, 2026 ... Padua to Venice (Full Day) Days: Wednesday | Friday | Saturday | Sunday ... 8:00 am → 05:30 pm ... €147 (adult) / €59 (child) ... Villa Foscari called 'La Malcontenta,' Villa Widmann, and Villa Pisani

claim: Castello del Catajo (Battaglia Terme) summer hours from May 2026: Tue-Thu 15:00-19:00, Sun 10:30-19:00, with extraordinary opening Tue 2 June.
quote: Summer Opening Hours (From May 2026): Tue – Wed – Thu: 3:00 pm – 7:00 pm; Sun: 10.30 am – 7:00 pm; Special Openings: Tue 2nd June: 10:30 am – 7:00 pm

claim: Villa dei Vescovi (FAI, Luvigliano di Torreglia) open Wed-Sun 10-18 from 14 Feb-4 Oct 2026; ticket €11 full / €6 reduced; free for FAI members; guided visits Sat-Sun at 11, 12, 15, 16.
quote: Dal 14 febbraio al 4 ottobre: mercoledì-domenica 10:00-18:00 ... Intero: €11,00 ... Ridotto: €6,00 ... Iscritti FAI: accesso gratuito

claim: Villa Widmann Rezzonico Foscari (Mira) opens Tue-Sun 10:00-13:00 and 13:30-16:30; ticket €7 full / €6 reduced; guided tour €10 with 24h reservation.
quote: Tuesday to Sunday ... 10:00-13:00 / 13:30-16:30 ... Entrance ticket: €7.00 full price, €6.00 reduced ... guided tour option available at €10.00 per person

claim: The Colli Euganei is one of Italy's few volcanic wine districts and the identity of the appellation is inseparable from Bordeaux varieties — Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc and Carménère — that have thrived for more than two centuries.
quote: The identity of the Colli Euganei is inseparable from its volcanic origins and the Bordeaux grape varieties—Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Cabernet Franc, and Carménère—that have thrived here for more than two centuries.

claim: The Euganean Hills rise 300–600m from the Padovan-Venetian plain and the vines are rooted in basaltic, mineral-rich soils that lend the wines depth and a distinctive savoury character.
quote: The vines are rooted in basaltic, mineral-rich soils, which lend the wines depth, structure, and a distinctive savory character.

claim: Colli Euganei Fior d'Arancio DOCG is Italy's only DOCG dedicated exclusively to aromatic Moscato Giallo, produced in still, sparkling and passito styles after promotion from DOC to DOCG in 2011.
quote: These sweet wines were sold under the Colli Euganei DOC title for a long time, but in 2011 their stand-out style and consistently high quality were officially recognised, and they were granted promotion to full, independent DOCG status.

claim: Vignalta in Arquà Petrarca, the largest producer of Colli Euganei DOC and Fior d'Arancio DOCG, is open Monday to Sunday 10:00–18:00 and offers a private tasting + cellar tour for €25 with 24-hour booking confirmation by email.
quote: Via Scalette 23, Arquà Petrarca, 35032, Italy ... Monday to Sunday from 10 am to 6 pm ... wineshop@vignalta.it

claim: Cantina Maeli in Baone runs three bookable tasting experiences focused on Moscato Giallo / Fior d'Arancio, with the standard tasting around €31.50–€35, rated 4.9 stars on Google.
quote: Welcome to Maeli ... Maeli Top Wine Tasting ... La via del Moscato giallo

claim: Ca' Lustra Zanovello in Faedo (Cinto Euganeo) offers a 'Classic Tasting' (4 wines plus cheese and bread) and a 'Deluxe Tasting' (guided vineyard + cellar tour with 6 wines), bookable daily in English for individuals or small groups.
quote: The Deluxe Tasting is a complete and exclusive experience that includes a guided tour through the vineyards and cellar, followed by tasting 6 wines

claim: Conte Emo Capodilista – La Montecchia in Selvazzano Dentro borders the Euganei park and is one of the closest serious estates to Rubano, owned by the family since the 15th century with 45 hectares of vines around the frescoed Villa Emo Capodilista.
quote: Via Montecchia 16 - 35030 Selvazzano Dentro (PD) ... La Montecchia welcomes those who want to organize tastings, holidays in the medieval town, in the castle or, exceptionally, in Villa Emo Capodilista, overlooking the vineyards.

claim: Borin Vini & Vigne sits in the Regional Park of the Colli Euganei between Monselice and Arquà Petrarca, with 26 of its 38 hectares planted to vines and 18 wines produced across four collections including a Fior d'Arancio DOCG.
quote: The Borin estate lies in the municipal areas of Monselice and Arquà Petrarca, in the Regional Nature Park of the Colli Euganei. Of the 38 hectares of land owned by the family, around 26 hectares are vineyards.

claim: Salvan – Vigne del Pigozzo conducts tastings personally led by the winemaker family (Giorgio, Rosanna, or Francesca), pouring at least 7 wines including indigenous Friularo and Turchetta.
quote: Through the tasting of at least 7 wines, visitors can discover the rich history of an area with a long winemaking tradition: going back to the time of the Venetians, with indigenous wines such as Friularo and Turchetta.

claim: Caffè Pedrocchi at Via VIII Febbraio 15 has operated for almost 200 years and serves its trademark coffee — espresso with mint cream and cocoa — which the house instructs you to drink without sugar or stirring.
quote: You shouldn't add any sugar nor stir it… Come and find out why!

claim: Pedrocchi opened in 1831 from Jappelli's neoclassical design and was nicknamed the 'café without doors' because it stayed open day and night until 1916; the Piano Nobile upstairs holds the Museum of the Risorgimento, ticket €4.
quote: From its inauguration in 1831 until 1916, it was always open, day and night, earning it the reputation of the "café without doors".

claim: Sotto il Salone, the covered market beneath the Palazzo della Ragione, has functioned continuously for nearly 800 years and houses more than fifty small shops selling cheeses, cured meats, wine and prepared food — the oldest covered shopping centre still in operation in Europe.
quote: the most ancient covered market in Europe ... more than fifty small shops offering quality food products such as cheeses, meats and cured meats from throughout Italy

claim: The open-air Piazza delle Erbe produce market runs Monday–Friday 07:00–13:30 and Saturday 07:30–20:00 with ~70 stalls of fruit, vegetables, legumes, cereals, flowers and seeds; closed Sunday.
quote: Monday-Friday: 7 am – 1:30 pm ... Saturday: 7:30 am – 8 pm ... approximately 70 stalls

claim: Padovan cuisine centres on gallina padovana (a dark-meat, crested heritage hen breed), bigoli (thick fresh spaghetti pushed through a bigolaro press), risi e bisi (spring rice and peas with pancetta), and bigoli with oca in onto (preserved goose).
quote: Bigoli are thick spaghetti prepared with flour, eggs, water and salt and then passed through a press called a bigolaro

claim: The Gallina Padovana breed is distinguished by a large head crest and beard with darker, more delicate meat than standard chicken, and is the basis of a classic local braise with tomato, onion, white wine and herbs.
quote: The breed is distinguished by the large crest that adorns the head and the beard under the beak, as well as for the meat which is darker than traditional chicken but more delicate and tasty.

claim: Aperol was created in 1919 by brothers Luigi and Silvio Barbieri and debuted at the Padova World Fair that year; the modern Prosecco-based spritz emerged in the 1970s and Veneto now consumes nearly 300,000 spritzes a day.
quote: Aperol came onto the scene in 1919, created by brothers Luigi and Silvio Barbieri in Padova. They debuted Aperol at the 1919 Padova World Fair.

claim: Padova's piazzas, arcades and historic centre are the canonical setting to drink spritz, which the city tourism board calls 'an undeniable part of Padova's life and atmosphere' and an official IBA cocktail since 2011.
quote: an undeniable part of Padova's life and atmosphere

claim: Veneto Euganei e Berici DOP olive oil is produced in 15 municipalities around the Euganean Hills Regional Park from Leccino and Rasara (minimum 50%) blended with Frantoio, Maurino and other local varieties.
quote: The oil is obtained from the Leccino and Rasara varieties (at least 50%) and the Frantoio, Maurino, Pendolino, Marzemino, Riondella, Trep or Drop or Matosso varieties

claim: Colli Euganei DOP olive oil shows an intense golden-green colour with a fruity aroma and low acidity, a product of the mild Euganean microclimate combined with volcanic soils — olive cultivation in the hills dates to the 15th-century Venetian Republic.
quote: Thanks to the combination of mild climate and volcanic soil, the extra virgin oil of Colli Euganei is one of the agricultural and food excellences of Veneto, appreciated for its harmonious taste and low acidity.

claim: Asparago Bianco di Bassano DOP — milk-white, fibreless, sweet-bitter — is harvested mid-March to mid-June, so a late-May visit hits peak season; classic Veneto preparations are risotto agli asparagi and asparagi con le uova.
quote: the production period goes from mid-March to mid-June

claim: The Festa dea Sarésa (Festa delle Ciliegie) in Zovon di Vo' Euganeo runs in 2026 across two weekends in late May: 22-24 and 29-31 May, with gastronomic stands, panini onti, live music and cherry-based products.
quote: 40th edition of the Festa delle Ciliegie at Zovon di Vo'. Dates: May 22, 23, 24, 29, 30, and 31, 2026 in Zovon di Vo' (Colli Euganei). Two weekends surrounded by lots of music, gastronomic stands with local specialties and the famous panini onti.

claim: The 'Ciliegie dei Colli Euganei' is a recognised Veneto PAT (Prodotto Agroalimentare Tradizionale) grown around Vo' Euganeo, with the cherry festival held annually in June and the cultivars including Bigarreau, Bigarreau Moreau, durona classica e precoce and durone di Vignola.
quote: Bigarreau, Bigarreau Moreau, durona classica e precoce, durone di Vignola, e altre spontanee della zona ... La 'Festa della ciliegia' si tiene ogni anno nel mese di giugno.

claim: The official Colli Euganei events portal lists the Festa delle Ciliegie at Zovon di Vò, organised by the Comune di Vo', with a gastronomic stand serving local specialties, wine and dolci alongside panini and beer.
quote: Zovon di Vò ... specialità locali, ottimo vino e dolci ... panini accompagnati da fiumi di birra ... promosso dal Comune di Vo'.
